ExplanationParts.CorpusEarnedOpening: Loud laughter is a narrated audible action assigned to the person who laughs, often closing or turning an encounter.
EvidenceBody: To laugh loudly—an audible “ha-ha” laugh recorded as an action in public encounters, sometimes followed by speech and sometimes serving as the whole turn. The exact phrase occurs 1,508 times in 278 allowlisted texts. The records preserve its range without assigning one fixed motive to it. Baizhang Huaihai laughs after a colleague asks why he had just cried and answers only, “Earlier I cried; now I laugh” . Zhaozhou Congshen laughs during an exchange and then repeats Hanshan's cry, “Heaven! Heaven!” . Jinniu Heshang dances with the rice tub, laughs loudly, and calls the assembly to eat . After an unnamed member of Baizhang's assembly reports returning to eat when he heard the meal drum, Baizhang laughs. Xiangshan Yunliang laughs after a pause and asks, “Laugh at what?” . Yuanwu Keqin laughs and then calls his own address speech about a dream where there is no dream and an affair where none exists. Dahui Zonggao laughs after an unnamed questioner answers by saying farewell and immediately tests the next entrant about that response. Zen preserves the laugh as a public-interview speaker-turn and teaching-seat action rather than reducing it to an editorial report about emotion.
